text: Continue strong reforms, thoroughly remove development bottlenecks: Prime Minister

On November 23, Prime Minister Le Minh Hung, along with the National Assembly delegation of Hai Phong city, met with voters in the northern port city after the 2nd session of the 16th National Assembly.
The conference was held both in-person and online, connecting to communes, wards, and special zones in the city.

At the conference, the Prime Minister, along with National Assembly delegates and city leaders, listened to, absorbed, and addressed the opinions and recommendations of voters regarding socio-economic development, institutional improvement, administrative reform, and social issues.

In his speech to the voters, Prime Minister Le Minh Hung emphasized the outstanding results of the 2nd session of the 16th National Assembly, particularly in legislative work, concretizing the Party's guidelines, improving policies and laws, and unlocking development resources.
According to the Prime Minister, institutional improvement is one of the prominent highlights in the activities of the National Assembly and the Government in recent times.

Strategic orientations and guidelines outlined by the 14th National Congress of the Party have been basically institutionalized in the first year of the Congress's 5-year term, thus creating a legal basis for implementation across all levels and sectors.

Meanwhile, the government focuses on building a comprehensive legal system, fostering development; addressing overlapping and conflicting regulations, creating a legal corridor for new business models and growth drivers.
Particularly, the work of decentralization, administrative reform, cutting, and simplifying business conditions has been vigorously implemented.

The Prime Minister affirmed that the Government will continue the spirit of strong reform on a large scale, continuously implementing and directing the thorough and effective removal of existing bottlenecks.
Regarding macroeconomics, the Government focuses on controlling inflation, stabilizing the currency value, and strengthening the stable foundation to promote high and sustainable growth.
In the first 10 months of 2026, the total amount of taxes, fees, and charges exempted, reduced, or extended reached VND366.6 trillion (more than $14.2 billion).
The total social investment capital in 9 months reached VND3.11 trillion, an increase of 15.1%.
Public investment disbursement reached nearly VND708.6 trillion, equivalent to 74.1% of the plan.
Notably, the Government has resolved and removed obstacles for 3,611 backlog projects, accounting for 72.8% of the projects needing resolution, with a total investment of over VND2.63 trillion.
Foreign investment attraction continues to be a highlight.
In 10 months, registered FDI capital reached $54.85 billion, up 74%; implemented capital reached $24.08 billion, up 13.1%.
Import and export turnover exceeded $1,000 billion for the first time.
State budget revenue for 10 months is estimated at VND2.44 drillion (nearly $94.7 billion), nearly 96.4% of the estimate, up 11% compared to the same period.

Along with economic development, the Government continues to focus on ensuring social welfare, improving people's living standards, and allocating resources for education, healthcare, and social policies.
The Prime Minister emphasized the need to shift strongly from policy to action and specific results, creating a solid foundation for growth throughout the term.

Identifying 2027 as a pivotal year for acceleration and breakthrough, the Prime Minister stated that the Government will focus on synchronously implementing solutions to mobilize resources and build an early growth scenario.
Accordingly, tasks and implementation progress will be specifically assigned to each field, ministry, sector, locality, and state enterprise; and adjusted monthly in line with actual developments.

Regarding growth drivers, the Government prioritizes the development of foundational industries, supporting industries, and new fields such as energy, materials, electronics, and semiconductors; promoting high-tech agriculture associated with deep processing, consumption, and export.

Along with that is the development of tourism, logistics, stimulating consumption, diversifying export markets; promoting the commercialization of research results, bringing science, technology, innovation, and digital transformation to become the main drivers of growth.

The Government continues to consolidate macroeconomic stability, control inflation, coordinate policies, ensure the supply of energy and essential goods, and reduce costs for businesses and the economy.

The Prime Minister particularly emphasized the urgent need to issue guiding documents for the implementation of laws and resolutions passed by the National Assembly; improve organizational effectiveness, and strengthen inspection and supervision.

At the same time, the Government will continue to improve the mechanism of decentralization and delegation associated with resource allocation, enhance the execution capacity of local governments, especially at the grassroots level; address obstacles in data connection, sharing, and administrative procedure resolution.

For Hai Phong, the Prime Minister acknowledged positive development results, with economic growth in 9 months reaching 12.08%, industrial production in 10 months increasing by 15.12%, and public investment disbursement by October 31 reaching 91.5%.
The Prime Minister suggested that the city continue striving to complete and exceed targets for GRDP growth, exports, budget revenue, public investment, and enterprise development.

The focus is on promoting administrative reform, removing difficulties for large projects; developing inter-regional infrastructure, connecting seaports, airports, enhancing logistics capacity; increasing domestic value in industry and the FDI sector, developing private enterprises and domestic suppliers.

In addition, the city needs to pay attention to investing in culture, education, healthcare, social housing, and rental housing, ensuring economic development associated with improving the quality of life for the people.

Regarding the 10 recommendations from voters, the Prime Minister affirmed that they will be absorbed with the highest sense of responsibility, directing the resolution of issues within the authority of the Government and the Prime Minister, ensuring clear progress, clear results, and reporting back to voters through the city's National Assembly delegation.

The recommendations focus on institutional improvement, special mechanisms for strategic urban areas, high-quality agricultural development, administrative reform, employment, housing, enhancing foreign language capacity, attracting talent, and connecting Vietnamese experts and scientists abroad.

On the afternoon of November 23, Prime Minister Le Minh Hung attended the groundbreaking ceremony for two major projects in Hai Phong, with a total investment of over VND26.4 trillion, aimed at developing seaport infrastructure, logistics, and high-tech industry.

The two projects include the construction of berths 9, 10, 11, and 12 at Lach Huyen Port Area and a factory for manufacturing pure materials for high-tech industries from clean rare earth materials at Xuan Cau Industrial Park and Free Trade Zone.

The Lach Huyen Port project has a total investment of nearly VND25 trillion VND, covering approximately 146.2 hectares of land and water, including 4 container berths with a total main wharf length of 1,800 meters, capable of receiving container ships from 12,000-18,000 TEUs.
The project contributes to enhancing cargo throughput capacity, developing logistics, and strengthening Hai Phong's position as an international seaport.

The pure material manufacturing factory project has an investment of nearly VND1.6 trillion, aimed at producing materials for high-tech industries such as electronics, energy, permanent magnets, and optics.
